newsitem.title: GABON: Cocoa producers to monitor output plan agreement.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa producers to monitor output plan agreement.

text.p: Cocoa producers broadly agree on output levels to meet International Cocoa Organisation target cuts and will set up a monitor to prevent overproduction by members, the Cocoa Producers Alliance said late on Friday.

"We want to be seen to be credible and serious movements in production in any region member's region will be reported to the CPA," said CPA President Matthew Nwagwu at the conclusion of the CPA General Asembly late on Friday.

The CPA has been meeting for the past four days to agree on new member output levels cutting the 1996/97 (from Oct 1) total by 90,000 tonnes over three years. The cut is part of an International Cocoa Organisation producer-consumer agreement made last month to help balance world supply and demand and is part of the 1993 International Cocoa Agreement production management plan.
"Ministers will decide on economic measures to keep members in line. This will include stopping new plantations." he added.
Cocoa producer ministers will arrive in Gabon on Monday for two days of talks to finalise CPA ouptut decisions and review the 1993 pact.
A response to European Union plans to raise non-cocoa fat usage will also be decided. Producers fear demand for cocoa beans could drop by 200,000 tonnes a year.
Ghana and Malaysia earlier this week asked for ICCO forecasts of their output to be revised before any cuts were applied, but the CPA's president said amounts disputed were minor.
"We have agreed levels in line with the ICCO for 1996/97," he said.
The CPA will also ask ministers to approve a slight budget increase over last year's $700,000.
Since Monday, the CPA has completed all productions, sales, finance and scientific committee work, said the president.
The CPA is organising a scientific conference in Santiago, Brazil on November 17-23, said Secretary-General Silas Kanga afterwards.
